record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.original_question: In the same B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map setting with smooth boundary data g of degree zero, let E(u)=integral_Omega |grad u|^2 on H^1_g(Omega; S^2). If the minimization is restricted to maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball, is the infimum of E achieved?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.2 ([40, 41]). Is the infimum of E(u) over H^1_g(Omega; S^2) intersect C(closed Omega) achieved?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the closed unit ball, and let $g : \partial \Omega \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree zero. Consider the Sobolev class
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u(x)| = 1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u|_{\partial\Omega} = g \},$$
equipped with the Dirichlet energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\, dx.$$
Let $C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2)$ denote the space of continuous $S^2$-valued maps on $\overline{\Omega}$. Determine whether the infimum
$$\inf\bigl\{ E(u) : u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2) \bigr\}$$
is attained by some map in $H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) \cap C(\overline{\Omega}; S^2)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Dirichlet energy attains its infimum within the class of continuous $S^2$-valued $H^1$ maps from $B^3$ with prescribed smooth degree-zero boundary data is a long-standing problem connected with the Hardt–Lin Lavrentiev gap phenomenon. The literature on harmonic maps with defects, Brezis–Coron–Lieb type results, and recent surveys on the Lavrentiev gap for harmonic maps into spheres continue to list this attainment question as open; no published proof of attainment or non-attainment was located.

status_evidence.title: The Lavrentiev gap phenomenon for harmonic maps into spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Hardt–Lin gap between the infimum of E over H^1_g and over its continuous subclass, for degree-zero boundary data.
status_evidence.claim: The continuous-class minimization problem remains a reference open question in this area.

status_evidence.title: A remark on H^1 mappings (Hardt–Lin)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs smooth degree-zero g for which the H^1 infimum is strictly less than the infimum among continuous competitors.
status_evidence.claim: Hardt–Lin established the strict gap but did not resolve attainment in the continuous class.
